statusText: Green. Weekend CME halt with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail at the low-band floor and mapped policy state EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Tail remains far below the block threshold. A narrow observation window is flagged around the 22:00 UTC Sunday futures reopen, when the hawkish post-Jackson-Hole repricing meets thin initial liquidity. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100: untested hawkish repricing sits behind a weekend futures halt; tail risk stays at the low-band floor into the Sunday reopen
body: The assessment is made during the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The verified anchor is Friday's close: NDX 29,433.43, down 0.70%, settling in the lower part of a 29,383.92-29,752.78 range, with VIX at 14.43. The dominant new information is policy-related rather than structural. Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks lifted September rate-hike odds from roughly 35% to near 57-60%, and the 2-year yield rose about 11 basis points to 4.34% in what JP Morgan data describes as the largest 2-year move after a Jackson Hole chair speech this century. The 10-year reached 4.72% and the 30-year 5.21%, a bear-flattening shape more consistent with policy repricing than with a growth shock; H.15 constant-maturity yields for 27 August stand at 4.20, 4.67 and 5.19 percent. Cross-asset alignment is only partial: short-end yields sharply higher against a calm VIX and a soft crude tape, with WTI at 83.44 dollars and Brent at 88.29 dollars after a weekly decline of roughly 4 percent as geopolitical transmission eased. Friday's index internals were rotational rather than directional, with semiconductors broadly lower (NVDA -4.57%, ARM -6.33%, INTC -2.85%) against gains in several megacaps (AMZN +3.97%, GOOGL +1.74%, MSFT +1.68%, AAPL +1.63%). Rotation of that kind normally reduces directional conviction rather than raising the probability of a persistent no-retracement path. Under the fixed mapping Tail 5 gives EA_ON and green. Stress is held at 25 to reflect an important repricing that has not yet been tested by any live tape, and Confidence at 72 reflects verified current levels, yields, oil, volatility and calendar coverage, bounded by the structural absence of a price path. A narrow danger window is flagged only across the 22:00 to 23:30 UTC reopen. The shared Finviz context file was approximately 4.7 hours old at assessment time and therefore stale under the inherited contract; its latest-session content was not relied upon, and the same internals were verified independently through primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment. The series was uniformly green with Tail held at 5 and dominant mode normal throughout, spanning Friday's US cash session, the Friday close and the weekend halt. Stress sat at 25-26 and Confidence decayed from 79 to 58 as the published evidence aged across the closed weekend, before recovering to 64 on the most recent refresh.
outlookSummary: The next 16 hours fall inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form and Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 25 to 29 as the reopen approaches. From the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen Tail is projected to lift to 12, still inside the low band, covering the first live test of near-coin-flip September rate-hike pricing, thin reopen liquidity and two-way gap risk. It then eases to 10-11 through the Asian session on expected volatility decay. Every post-reopen structure is stated conditionally because none of it is observable now. Monday 31 August brings month-end flows and a UK bank holiday that conditionally thins the European handover, and the data-heavy week beyond the horizon starts with ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on 1 September and runs to Nonfarm Payrolls on 4 September. Mapped policy state stays EA_ON across all 24 projected hours.
